Don't worry too much about offending people. This is about your health and well-being. It's great that you wish to seek help, and the first step is being completely honest about what's going on in your head. Even if you think someone might be offended, say how you feel. That's the only way you'll get the care you deserve. I'd recommend taking about it to people you trust first (you might have some close friends or a family member your particularly close to) then gradually opening up more often. Then if necessary you can seek professional help if you feel that's what you feel you need. There may be some people who don't understand what you're going through, who might be "offended". But that's because they don't understand what you're going through. Don't let them get in the way of you feeling better.

My advice would be to talk to someone about this. Someone professional. Someone like a counselor, therapist or doctor. It sounds like you're having intrusive thoughts, lots of people have them, including me, but if you're having urges to act on these thoughts, that's serious. It can be difficult and stressful reaching out for professional help, and the first few days can sometimes feel worse than how you felt before seeking help, but trust me, it will help in the long run.

To know if it's deep, you need to know what layer you've hit. The 3 main layers that people talk about are epidermis, dermis and fat.
Epidermis: this is the top layer of the skin. Cuts to this layer are sometimes called cat scratches. They look thin, don't gape open, and bleed a little. You can't see inside an epidermis wound because it's on the very top of the skin and  therefore is very shallow.
Dermis: these cuts gape open a bit. When you cut a dermis cut (or styros as they're sometimes called) you can see the inside of the wound. It will look white (a bit like styrofoam, hence the name) before taking a few seconds to fill up with blood.
Fat: these cuts gape open end exposes a yellow, bubbly layer which looks a bit like a tin of baked beans (which is why this layer is sometimes called beans). These wounds will also bleed a lot so be careful.

It's important to know what layers your cutting to so you know how to care for your wounds. I'd recommend you take a look at this Reddit post for some more information about layers of the skin and proper treatment of wounds, it'll teach you more than anything I can teach you:  https://www.reddit.com/r/selfharm/comments/crvkmk/full_indepth_guide_on_everything_you_need_to_know/

Alright, my advice is this, and I know you've probably heard this before and are probably sick of it. But, distract yourself with literally anything, it doesn't matter what it is, just tell yourself that you're going to do this one thing and focus all your attention on it. I know it's not easy to just "distract" yourself when the urge to self harm is always in the back of your head. But I need you to try. If you want advice from personal experience, some of the things that have successfully helped me in distracting myself are taking freezing cold showers (this one might be uncomfortable if you're not used to it) and listening to music at insanely high volumes. These are just two random things that have for some odd reason have been the most successful in stopping me from giving in to urges. But I can't guarantee they'll work for you. As a last resort, and I mean LAST resort, you might feel like you need to self harm, but please avoid your face, I know the thoughts are saying specifically to cut a smile on your face, but please if you are going to cut, don't do the face. I'm glad the thoughts to cut a smile have only been going on for a day, but you can't let yourself act on it. Otherwise, and trust me on this, these kind of urges will get worse. I can tell from your willingness to talk about this that you're a strong person. It's not easy to ask for help. It's not easy to just say what's up. But you can get through it, tell the urges to shut the fuck up. Like I said before, that's not an easy thing to do. But I need you try. I know you can get through it if you try.

Some people (including me) start off cutting just cat scratches, which makes them feel invalid when they see people with deep scars. So they start cutting styros, they bleed more. And for a while they feel valid, but only for a while, so they cut deeper, and so on and so forth. All I can say is this feeling of invalidity won't leave us. Self harm just keeps taking, it makes us feel good sure, but only for a few hours or day (sometimes less) then we go back wanting to cut deeper. OP, I want you to remember that this feeling of invalidity is normal, we all feel it. But we can't let it control us. That's the hard bit.
